issues.description: Constructor parameter order for class Meal is inconsistent: The problem statement UML and the solution implementation declare the constructor as Meal(String name, String[] ingredients), but the template implementation declares the constructor as Meal(String[] ingredients, String name). Additionally, example usage in the template Main (new Meal("cowBoyStew", new String[]{...})) uses the (String name, String[] ingredients) order, which will not match the template constructor and will cause compilation errors and confusion for students.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the template Meal constructor to use the parameter order (String name, String[] ingredients) to match the UML and the solution. Change the constructor signature to: public Meal(String name, String[] ingredients) { this.name = name; this.ingredients = ingredients; }. Also ensure any example usages in Main and other template files use the same parameter order (name first, ingredients second).

issues.description: Constructor parameter order mismatch for the Meal class: the problem statement UML and the solution implement Meal(String name, String[] ingredients) and the Main usage examples construct meals as new Meal("name", new String[]{...}). However, the template implementation declares the constructor as public Meal(String[] ingredients, String name) (parameters reversed). This prevents students from using the example code and from matching the UML/solution constructor signature, causing confusion when instantiating Meal objects.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the template with the UML and solution by changing the constructor in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Meal.java to public Meal(String name, String[] ingredients) and update the constructor body to assign this.name = name; this.ingredients = ingredients;. This preserves the problem statement examples and matches the solution implementation.
